rules.name: Google Chrome leftovers
rules.description: Profile data, caches and preferences left behind by Google Chrome.

provenance.source: Observed install of Google Chrome on macOS 26 (2026-10-16); generic locations: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/FileManagement/Conceptual/FileSystemProgrammingGuide/MacOSXDirectories/MacOSXDirectories.html
provenance.author: lapht
provenance.rationale: Chrome stores its profiles in Application Support/Google/Chrome and its disk cache in Caches/Google/Chrome. Only the Chrome subfolders are listed: the parent Google folders are shared with Chrome Beta, Dev, Canary and Google Updater and are never proposed. Generic per-bundle-ID locations (Caches, Preferences plist, Saved Application State, HTTPStorages, WebKit) are where macOS frameworks store data keyed by the app's bundle ID; they are matched only when they exist.

rules.name: Visual Studio Code leftovers
rules.description: Settings, caches and preferences left behind by Visual Studio Code.

provenance.source: Observed install of Visual Studio Code on macOS 26 (2026-10-16); generic locations: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/FileManagement/Conceptual/FileSystemProgrammingGuide/MacOSXDirectories/MacOSXDirectories.html
provenance.author: lapht
provenance.rationale: VS Code stores user data in Application Support/Code (Insiders uses a separate 'Code - Insiders' folder) and its updater state in Caches/com.microsoft.VSCode.ShipIt. ~/.vscode is outside the leftover roots and is not covered. Generic per-bundle-ID locations (Caches, Preferences plist, Saved Application State, HTTPStorages, WebKit) are where macOS frameworks store data keyed by the app's bundle ID; they are matched only when they exist.

rules.name: Bitwarden leftovers
rules.description: Sandbox containers and the app group container left behind by Bitwarden.

provenance.source: Observed install of Bitwarden on macOS 26 (2026-10-16); generic locations: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/FileManagement/Conceptual/FileSystemProgrammingGuide/MacOSXDirectories/MacOSXDirectories.html; app group from the app's com.apple.security.application-groups entitlement
provenance.author: lapht
provenance.rationale: Bitwarden is sandboxed, so its data lives in its container. The loginhelper and safari containers belong to the login item and Safari extension embedded in Bitwarden.app. The group container LTZ2PFU5D6.com.bitwarden.desktop is declared in the app's application-groups entitlement and is marked shared.

provenance.author: lapht
provenance.rationale: The Unarchiver is sandboxed and declares no app group, so all of its data lives in its own container. Group containers of other apps from the same developer team are not listed.

rules.name: Gradle caches
rules.description: Finds downloaded dependencies and build caches in Gradle's user home.

provenance.source: https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/directory_layout.html#dir:gradle_user_home
provenance.author: lapht
provenance.rationale: Gradle re-downloads dependencies and rebuilds its caches on demand. Only the caches subfolder is listed: wrapper distributions, gradle.properties and init scripts in ~/.gradle are never proposed.

rules.name: Maven local repository
rules.description: Finds the Maven local repository. Artifacts installed locally with mvn install may not be re-downloadable; never preselected.

provenance.source: https://maven.apache.org/guides/introduction/introduction-to-repositories.html
provenance.author: lapht
provenance.rationale: Downloaded artifacts are re-fetched from remote repositories, but artifacts put there by mvn install (local builds, private snapshots) may exist nowhere else, so the user must opt in explicitly and sees a warning. Only the repository folder is listed: settings.xml and toolchains.xml in ~/.m2 are never proposed.

rules.name: Cargo registry cache
rules.description: Finds downloaded crate archives and extracted crate sources in Cargo's registry.

provenance.source: https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/cargo-home.html
provenance.author: lapht
provenance.rationale: Cargo re-downloads crate archives (cache) and re-extracts them (src) on the next build. The registry index, installed binaries in ~/.cargo/bin and credentials are never proposed.

rules.name: Go module cache
rules.description: Finds downloaded Go modules in the module cache.

provenance.source: https://go.dev/ref/mod#module-cache
provenance.author: lapht
provenance.rationale: The Go module cache is rebuilt from the module proxy on demand. Only pkg/mod is listed: the go-build cache is already covered by the ~/Library/Caches scan, and ~/go/bin and ~/go/src are never proposed.

rules.name: Bun install cache
rules.description: Finds Bun's global package cache.

provenance.source: https://bun.sh/docs/install/cache
provenance.author: lapht
provenance.rationale: Bun repopulates its global install cache on the next bun install. Installed binaries in ~/.bun/bin are never proposed.

rules.name: uv cache
rules.description: Finds uv's downloaded and built Python package cache.

provenance.source: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/cache/
provenance.author: lapht
provenance.rationale: uv documents its cache as safe to remove; it is rebuilt on demand. The pip, Poetry and CocoaPods caches live in ~/Library/Caches and are covered by that scan, so they are not repeated here.

rules.name: conda package cache
rules.description: Finds downloaded conda packages in the pkgs folder of common conda installs.

provenance.source: https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/stable/user-guide/tasks/manage-pkgs.html
provenance.author: lapht
provenance.rationale: conda keeps downloaded tarballs and extracted packages in pkgs and re-downloads them when needed. Only pkgs folders are listed: environments (envs) are never proposed.
